name: Marvis Virtual Network Assistant
description: One of the earliest and most mature entries in this space. Marvis sits on top of Juniper's Mist AI telemetry and answers plain-language questions about wired, wireless, and SD-WAN health. "Marvis Actions" goes further and proactively remediates common issues: bad cables, missing VLANs, DHCP and 802.1X failures. "Marvis Minis" continuously simulate client connections in the background so problems surface before a real user hits them.
search: marvis virtual network assistant vna hpe juniper networks mist ai wireless wired sd-wan marvis actions minis

name: Cisco AI Assistant for Networking
description: A conversational layer across Catalyst Center and the Meraki dashboard, built on retrieval-augmented generation against Cisco's own documentation and telemetry, with filters aimed at catching hallucinated answers. The more interesting pieces are narrower: AI-RRM schedules radio channel changes during actual quiet hours instead of reacting to every blip, and an AI-driven packet analyzer can trigger its own captures and hand back a root cause instead of a raw pcap.
search: cisco ai assistant for networking catalyst center meraki ai-rrm packet analyzer thousandeyes rag

name: AVA (Autonomous Virtual Assist)
description: Built on Arista's Network Data Lake, AVA's core trick is learning what "normal" looks like across a fleet so it can narrow in on the small residue of anomalous behavior rather than every deviation. That same approach has been extended into AI data center fabrics, watching ECN marks, PFC pause frames, and buffer utilization on GPU clusters. In the campus and SD-WAN side, "Ask AVA" translates zero-trust segmentation policy into plain language.
search: arista ava autonomous virtual assist eos netdl ai data center ai fabric ask ava velocloud zero trust

name: Extreme AI Expert
description: Part of Extreme Platform ONE, positioned as a multimodal conversational agent spanning both networking and security tasks instead of staying in one lane. Newer to market than Marvis or AVA, so the feature set is worth watching mature before taking the launch materials at face value.
search: extreme ai expert extreme networks platform one multimodal conversational

name: FlowAI & Intelligent Agents
description: The interesting design choice here is architectural: the AI never gets to actually touch the network. It proposes a workflow, and a separate deterministic orchestration layer enforces approvals, schedules the change into a maintenance window, executes it, validates the result, and rolls back automatically if something fails. It's one of the clearer answers to "how do you let a language model near production without losing control."
search: itential flowai intelligent agents agentic operations for infrastructure deterministic orchestration governance rollback

name: Selector Copilot
description: A multi-domain observability platform with a "network language model" front end, ingesting SNMP, gRPC, NetFlow, BGP, and syslog data. Engineers query across all of it in plain language instead of a proprietary query syntax.
search: selector ai copilot network language model nlm mcp observability

name: Edwin AI
description: A narrower, ITOps-focused agent aimed squarely at alert fatigue: consolidating and reasoning across infrastructure alarms so a human sees one correlated incident instead of forty related pages.
search: edwin ai logicmonitor incident management alert noise reduction itops

name: AI Control Tower
description: Aimed at telecom operators rather than enterprise networks: a control plane concept meant to connect business intent, risk, and network execution across OSS, BSS, and CRM systems. More of an emerging architecture than a single deployable product today.
search: servicenow ai control tower autonomous networks telecom intent oss bss crm

name: Fabrix.ai Network Observability
description: A vendor-agnostic observability layer, not a single-purpose agent: it ingests network, application, and infrastructure telemetry through more than a thousand pre-built connectors (Cisco, Juniper, Arista, Prometheus, Datadog, and more), correlates events across domains to find root cause, and can trigger closed-loop remediation through Ansible, Python, or Cisco NSO playbooks.
search: fabrix network observability data fabric rdaf telemetry pipeline multi-vendor closed-loop remediation ansible cisco nso

name: Precision AI / Strata Copilot
description: Powers Palo Alto's Cloud-Delivered Security Services with purpose-built security models rather than a general-purpose LLM, aimed at automated threat detection, zero-trust enforcement, and DNS/URL filtering at the speed those decisions need to happen.
search: precision ai strata copilot palo alto networks zero trust dns url filtering cdss

name: FortiAI
description: Embedded in FortiAnalyzer, aimed at incident investigation and response: summarizing security events, estimating impact, and suggesting remediation so SOC analysts spend less time on triage and more on the incidents that matter.
search: fortiai fortinet fortianalyzer soc incident triage threat intelligence

name: Network Change Risk Assessment Agent
description: Scores the blast radius and rollback safety of a proposed network change before it goes out. Category: NetOps.
search: fabrix network change risk assessment agent blast radius rollback

name: Network Config Compliance Agent
description: Checks device configurations against vendor guidelines and internal best practices on an ongoing basis. Category: NetOps.
search: fabrix network config compliance agent best practices vendor guidelines

name: RCA for Networking Issues Agent
description: Investigates the likely root cause of a networking issue within a given time window and suggests remediation. Category: NetOps.
search: fabrix rca for networking issues root cause analysis

name: Anomaly Detection Agent
description: Learns baselines from metrics and logs and surfaces real-time deviations. Category: AIOps.
search: fabrix anomaly detection agent baseline metrics logs real time

name: SecOps Incident Manager
description: Automates incident handling: opens tickets, notifies the right people, and keeps the loop closed. Category: SecOps.
search: fabrix secops incident manager servicenow slack tickets

name: CVE Vulnerability Analyst Agent
description: Rather than listing every CVE that touches installed software, cross-references known CVEs against the current network topology to estimate real exposure. Category: Cybersecurity.
search: fabrix cve vulnerability analyst agent topology exposure

name: NetClaw
description: Built on OpenClaw, one of the largest open source agent frameworks, NetClaw specializes it for network engineering: CLI/NETCONF skills, growing MCP integrations, and a Border/Member architecture delegating tasks to specialized sub-agents. One of the most visible, fastest-moving projects in this space, but still effectively a one-maintainer effort with no independent security review, and its own federation scheme (NCFED) is an individual IETF draft, not an adopted standard.
search: netclaw openclaw automateyournetwork federation ncfed hermes claude bgp multiplexed
